If your priority is purely putting the most cash into your bank account, the 'Most Income' plan (Soybeans -> Grain Sorghum (Milo) -> Soybeans) delivers $39,245.51 in clear net profit. If your ground is tired and you want to restore soil vitality, the 'Best Soil Health' plan (Alfalfa (Lucerne) -> Winter Wheat -> Alfalfa (Lucerne)) fixes 229 kg of free nitrogen out of the air and softens hardpan compaction. gemini_advisory.three_year_operational_overview:
3-YEAR OPERATIONAL ROADMAP:
- Year 1 (Foundation & Setup): Test topsoil nutrients, adjust tractor tire pressure to 12-15 PSI to avoid hardpan packing, and calibrate seeding drills. Plant the primary crop on time to establish early canopy cover.
- Year 2 (Biological Transition): Rotate crop families to break weed and pest cycles. If planting legumes, verify rhizobia seed inoculant. Scout for moisture drawdown during midsummer heat.
- Year 3 (Harvest & Handover): Cut synthetic fertilizer rates by the full legume credit left in the soil. Conduct a simple spade test at harvest to inspect earthworm channels and root depth before deciding the next cycle.

gemini_advisory.farmer_decision_guide:
WHICH PLAN SHOULD YOU CHOOSE?
1. Choose 'Most Income' if: You have cash in the bank, market contracts in hand, and want maximum total dollars.
2. Choose 'Highest ROI' if: You have limited working capital and need each dollar to generate the biggest percentage return.
3. Choose 'Best Soil Health' if: Your ground is compacted (>250 PSI), organic matter is low, and you want to build long-term land equity.
4. Choose 'Least Effort' if: You farm part-time, have older machinery, or cannot afford hired labor.
5. Choose 'Least Crop Loss Risk' if: Your area suffers from erratic rainfall, heat spikes, and you want guaranteed security.
ground_truth_field_checklist: Dig a simple spade test hole (30 cm deep) to inspect earthworm activity and check for hardpan layers.
Set tractor and combine tire pressures to 12-15 PSI before field entry to prevent deep soil packing.
Verify live rhizobia inoculant on all legume seed bags before planting (store in cool, dark place).
Walk field boundaries and drainage ditches after the first heavy rain to ensure water runs off without pooling.
Calibrate seed drill meters and sprayer nozzles with clean water to avoid costly over-application.
Take a quick mid-season soil moisture check at shovel depth during peak summer flowering.
